title: The system design interview framework

kcs.statement: A system design interview answer moves through fixed steps in order: requirements, estimation, API, data model, high-level design, deep dive, then bottlenecks and trade-offs.
Drawing components before agreeing on requirements is the most common failure, because every later choice (store, cache, sharding) depends on the agreed scope and scale.

problem_ideas: Put eight shuffled interview steps (API, estimates, deep dive, requirements…) into the correct order
A candidate opens 'design Instagram' by drawing Kafka and Cassandra: name the step they skipped and what it costs them
Given a transcript excerpt, label which framework step each paragraph belongs to
Interviewer says 'assume 100M users' at minute 20: which earlier steps must be revisited?
Rewrite a rambling first two minutes of an answer into a framework-led opening
Decide which step to cut short when only 30 minutes are available instead of 45
